skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Reviews local changes and GitHub pull requests for correctness, maintainability, security, test coverage, and project standards.
skill.summary: Guides structured code reviews for local diffs and remote pull requests.
skill.author: google-gemini

security_audit.summary: I confirmed the external command risk for GitHub PR checkout and npm preflight execution, especially on remote PR branches. Several static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline branch names, or hardcoded read-only git inspection commands. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden semantic abuse was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote PR checkout uses an external GitHub CLI command.
remediation.suggestion: Validate pull request identifiers and ask before changing branches or checking out untrusted code.

remediation.issue: Remote preflight can run package scripts from a pull request branch.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running package scripts from PR branches and document the trust boundary.

remediation.issue: Local optional preflight can execute project scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Keep user confirmation mandatory and warn that package scripts may execute arbitrary code from the workspace.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes and Pull Requests
content.value_statement: Manual code reviews can miss defects, test gaps, and risky changes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured local and pull request reviews.
actual_capabilities: Selects a review target from a pull request number, URL, or local changes.
Guides remote pull request checkout with the GitHub CLI.
Inspects local repository status, working tree diffs, and staged diffs.
Evaluates correctness, maintainability, readability, efficiency, security, error handling, and tests.
Organizes feedback into summary, findings, severity groups, and a clear recommendation.
limitations: Requires working git context for local change review.
Remote pull request review depends on the GitHub CLI and repository access.
Project preflight commands can execute package scripts and need user approval.
Findings are review guidance and do not guarantee complete vulnerability coverage.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Inspect local staged and unstaged changes before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Assess a Remote Pull Request
use_cases.description: Checkout a pull request, read its context, run approved checks, and prepare actionable feedback.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Coverage
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to evaluate tests, error handling, performance, and security concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Local Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current local changes. Check correctness, maintainability, tests, and security. Start with git status and diff, then list findings by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Review Staged Changes Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Review only my staged changes. Focus on release risk, missing tests, and user-visible behavior changes. Do not run preflight unless I approve it.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pull Request by Number
prompt_templates.prompt: Review PR #123. Checkout the pull request, read its description, run approved project checks, and provide an approved or request changes recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintainer review of a remote contribution

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Risk-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied pull request with extra attention to authentication, data handling, migration safety, and rollback paths. Explain each blocking finding with evidence.

output_examples.input: Review my local changes before I open a pull request.
output: Summary: The change is mostly ready, but one edge case lacks coverage.
Improvements: Add a regression test for empty input and document the new validation branch.
Conclusion: Request changes until the missing test is added.

output_examples.input: Review PR #42 for security and reliability risk.
output: Summary: The pull request improves validation but changes a sensitive path.
Critical: One authorization check needs stronger evidence before approval.
Improvements: Add a failure-path test and clarify the migration rollback plan.

output_examples.input: Review only the staged changes for maintainability.
output: Summary: The staged changes are small and easy to follow.
Improvements: Extract the repeated condition into a named helper.
Nitpicks: Align the new test names with the existing style.
Conclusion: Approved after the maintainability improvement.

best_practices: Confirm before running project scripts on untrusted branches.
Provide the review goal, changed area, and expected behavior.
Ask for severity-ordered findings with file and line references when available.
anti_patterns: Running package scripts from unknown pull requests without explicit approval.
Using the skill as a replacement for human approval on high-risk changes.
Requesting broad reviews without sharing the target branch, pull request, or diff scope.

faq.question: Can it review local changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide review of working tree changes, staged changes, or both.

faq.question: Can it review remote pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports pull request numbers or URLs when GitHub CLI access is available.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: It may guide git and project check commands. Approve package scripts only when you trust the workspace.

faq.question: Does it replace continuous integration?
faq.answer: No. It complements automated checks by adding human-style reasoning and focused feedback.

faq.question: Can it find security issues?
faq.answer: It includes security review as one checklist area, but it is not a full security audit.

faq.question: What tools work with this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
